claims.statement: The checkout documents three launch recipes that all invoke the same `main()` of `src/StartJetty.java`: running the class from an IDE with the working directory set to the project root, `java -cp "web/WEB-INF/lib/*" src/StartJetty.java` from the project root on JDK 11+, and the JDK 8 fallback `javac -encoding UTF-8 -cp "web/WEB-INF/lib/*" -d web/WEB-INF/classes src/StartJetty.java` followed by `java -cp "web/WEB-INF/lib/*:web/WEB-INF/classes" StartJetty`; none of them needs a build step, an installed servlet container or an installed database.

`locateProjectRoot()` identifies the project root by the presence of `web/WEB-INF/web.xml`, walking up to four parents from the JVM working directory and then up to six parents from `StartJetty`'s code-source location, and aborts the launch with an `IllegalStateException` instructing the operator to set the working directory to the project root when neither walk finds it.

A healthy start prints a banner naming the three addresses — `http://localhost:8080/`, `http://localhost:8080/admin_category_list`, `http://localhost:8082` — together with the H2 console JDBC URL and the `sa`/empty-password credentials, and the banner is printed only after `server.start()` returns, so a launch that fails earlier (for example on a taken port) produces no banner.

Both service ports and the context path are compile-time constants in the launcher (`PORT = 8080`, `H2_CONSOLE_PORT = 8082`, `CONTEXT_PATH = "/"`), so changing a port is a Java edit plus a restart rather than a configuration option, and the banner, `STARTUP.md` and the acceptance record all name the same addresses.

The first start takes about 5–8 seconds because `ensureCompiledClasses()` compiles every `.java` file under `src/` into `web/WEB-INF/classes` and synchronises non-Java resources on every launch, and the `dbInit` bean executes the seed script during the Spring context refresh.

The launcher aborts before any port is bound when the project root or `src/` cannot be found, or when the in-process compilation of `src/` fails; the corresponding messages are `找不到源码目录 src/` and `源码编译失败，请查看上方编译错误`, with each `Diagnostic.Kind.ERROR` streamed as `[StartJetty] 编译错误: …`.

On a JRE (`ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler()` returns `null`) the launcher prints `[StartJetty] 当前是 JRE 环境，跳过编译，直接使用 web/WEB-INF/classes 已有产物` and returns early, skipping both compilation and resource synchronisation and using whatever classes already exist in the git-ignored `web/WEB-INF/classes` directory.

The H2 console runs as a second, independent web server on port 8082 and is deliberately not mounted inside the application, because the Struts2 filter mapped to `/*` in `web/WEB-INF/web.xml` hands any in-app console path to the dispatcher, which answers `no action mapped`.

The console login parameters are JDBC URL `jdbc:h2:mem:tmall_ssh;MODE=MySQL;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1`, user `sa` and an empty password, matching the datasource bean in `src/applicationContext.xml`; `DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1` keeps the in-memory database alive for the JVM's lifetime, which is why the console can read the application's business data while an H2 console started outside this JVM cannot.

The database is pure in-memory and every start re-executes `classpath:sql/tmall_ssh_h2.sql` through the `dbInit` bean, so all data is discarded when the process stops and restarting is the way to return to the seeded demo state.

`sf` declares `depends-on="dbInit"` so the seed script always runs before Hibernate or any DAO query starts; removing either the `dbInit` bean or that attribute leaves the schema uncreated and surfaces as `Table "XXX" not found`.

The seed script is create-only — nine plain `CREATE TABLE` statements, the demo INSERTs and a trailing `ALTER TABLE … ALTER COLUMN id RESTART WITH n` calibration (`category=84`, `product=963`, `productimage=10211`, `property=258`, `propertyvalue=14092`) — with no `DROP TABLE` or `IF NOT EXISTS`, so it assumes a fresh empty database and the calibration keeps first-insert ids aligned with the original MySQL `AUTO_INCREMENT`.

Stopping is `Ctrl+C` or otherwise terminating the process: `server.setStopAtShutdown(true)` registers a JVM shutdown hook that stops Jetty and its handlers in the normal order, `server.join()` is what keeps the process alive, and there is no stop endpoint, reload or watchdog.
The documented recovery for a taken port is `lsof -ti:8080,8082 | xargs kill` followed by a relaunch from the project root, targeting both ports because the launcher binds 8080 and 8082.

A corrupted dependency jar surfaces as `zip END header not found`; the repair is re-downloading that artefact from the public mirror `https://maven.aliyun.com/repository/public/`, and the batch integrity check is `for f in web/WEB-INF/lib/*.jar; do unzip -tq "$f" >/dev/null || echo "$f 损坏"; done`.

The JSP failures `getTldCache() is null` and `TldCache cannot be cast` (webapp unavailable) are caused by modifying the explicit `Configuration[]` chain or the `addSystemClass` list in `src/StartJetty.java`, the two blocks `STARTUP.md` tells readers not to change.

The `PROPERTYVALUE FOREIGN KEY(PID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(ID)` referential-integrity warning was produced by `hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=update` auto-creating foreign keys that the original MySQL schema lacked, and it no longer appears because the property is now `none` with the schema owned by the seed script; the `STARTUP.md` troubleshooting row still lists that warning as harmless.

Logging output normally goes to the console through a root `INFO` appender with pattern `[%-5p] %d %c - %m%n`; a `File` appender writes `dist/my.log` relative to the process working directory but is attached only to the logger `mh.sample2.Log4jTest2`, which no class in `src/` uses, and `dist/` plus `*.log` are git-ignored.

Environment requirements are a JDK only — JDK 8, 11 or 17 all run the project, JDK 17 (Temurin 17.0.20.1) is the recorded verification environment, and neither Tomcat nor MySQL has to be installed because Jetty 9.4.58 and H2 1.4.200 are vendored among the 65 jars in `web/WEB-INF/lib`.

The documented commands are POSIX-shell shaped (the JDK 8 fallback separates classpath entries with `:` and the failure recipes use `lsof`, `xargs`, `unzip -tq` and a `for … done` loop) while the launcher itself is path-agnostic, resolving everything from the discovered project root, and the IDE metadata's dead Windows absolute paths were replaced by per-jar references under `web/WEB-INF/lib`.
